newsitem.title: USA: Waste Management shareholder applauds new chairman.
newsitem.headline: Waste Management shareholder applauds new chairman.

text.p: Soros Fund Management, which holds about 5.8 percent of Waste Management Inc's shares, on Monday applauded the company for hiring a Sprint Corp executive to be Waste Management's chairman, president and chief executive officer.
Waste Management named Ronald LeMay, president and chief operating officer of Sprint, to head the company.

Earlier this year, pressure from financier George Soros and his Soros Fund Management helped pressure Phillip Rooney to resign as chief executive officer of WMX Technologies, the former name of Waste Management Inc.
Dean Buntrock, Waste Management's founding chairman, will remain a member of the board.

"Soros Fund Management congratulates the board of directors of Waste Management on securing Ron LeMay who, we believe, will be an outstanding chief executive officer," Stanley Druckenmiller, chief investment strategist at Soros Fund Management, said in a statement.

"Mr. LeMay's impressive track record at Sprint, including his turning around the long distance business in the early 1990's, makes us confident that he has the leadership qualities to realize the value we believe is inherent in Waste Management's business," he added.

LeMay had joined Sprint in 1985 and held several executive positions including president and chief operating officer of Sprint's long distance division and president and chief operating officer of Sprint PCS. He was named president and chief operating officer of Sprint in February 1996.

"It is our understanding that Mr. LeMay's considerable compensation package is tied to the performance of Waste Management, and thus we are pleased that his interests are aligned with those of all shareholders," Druckenmiller said.
A Waste Management spokesman could not be reached to comment on LeMay's compensation package.
